sections.heading: Content
sections.wikitext: The song is about a woman who advises an unfaithful mate: "The angel in your arms this morning is gonna be the devil in someone else's arms tonight," meaning that she has assuaged his neglect and infidelities by indulging in illicit trysts of her own.

sections.heading: Hot version
sections.wikitext:
Although "Angel in Your Arms" belongs to the tradition of cheating songs prevalent in [[country music]], the song was introduced by pop/R&B act Hot on their self-titled debut album, recorded in 1976 at Wishbone Studios in [[Muscle Shoals, Alabama]] with Wishbone's owners Clayton Ivey and Terrence (Terry) Woodford producing.<ref name="Guitar Towns">{{cite book
| first= Randy
| last= McNutt
| year= 2002
| title= Guitar Towns: a journey to the crossroads of rock 'n' roll
| publisher= Indiana University Press
| location= Bloomington, IN
| page= [https://archive.org/details/guitartownsjourn00mcnu/page/140 140]
| isbn= 0-253-34058-6
| url-access= registration
| url= https://archive.org/details/guitartownsjourn00mcnu/page/140
}}</ref> It was Hot's lead singer Gwen Owens who requested the group be given a country song, and Ivey and Woodford obliged with "Angel in Your Arms", whose third co-writer was Muscle Shoals resident Tom (Tommy) Brasfield.
<ref name="Alabama Hall of Fame">
{{cite web|url=http://www.alamhof.org/tommybrasfield.html |title=Alabama Hall of Fame |website=Alamhof.org |accessdate=15 February 2010 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20101025133005/http://alamhof.org/tommybrasfield.html |archivedate=25 October 2010 }}</ref>
<ref name="AMG">
{{cite web|url=http://allmusic.com/|title=AMG|accessdate=15 February 2010| archiveurl= https://web.archive.org/web/20100211203629/http://www.allmusic.com/| archivedate= 11 February 2010 | url-status= live}}</ref> Although Hot was officially a trio consisting of Owens, Cathy Carson, and Juanita Curiel, Owens has stated that she recorded "Angel in Your Arms" with only Carson as background vocalist: Irene Cathaway, with whom Owens and Carson had been performing and who was expected to record with them at Muscle Shoals, was a no-show at the recording studio, and "Angel in Your Arms" was recorded prior to the recruitment of Curiel as Cathaway's replacement.<ref>{{cite book| first=Bob| last=Leszczak| title=Encyclopedia of Pop Music Aliases 1950-2000| year=2015| publisher=Rowman & Littlefied| location=Lanham MD| page=163| isbn=978-1442240070}}</ref>  Ivey played keyboards on Hot's recording of "Angel in Your Arms", which featured [[Mac McAnally]] on guitar.
At the time of Hot's success with their single version, the group also recorded a Spanish-language version entitled "Angel en Tus Brazos".<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.discogs.com/Hot-Angel-En-Tus-Brazos/release/1075097 |title=Hot - Angel En Tus Brazos (Vinyl) at Discogs |year=1977 |publisher=Discogs.com |accessdate=2014-08-04}}</ref>
sections.text:
Although "Angel in Your Arms" belongs to the tradition of cheating songs prevalent in country music, the song was introduced by pop/R&B act Hot on their self-titled debut album, recorded in 1976 at Wishbone Studios in Muscle Shoals, Alabama with Wishbone's owners Clayton Ivey and Terrence (Terry) Woodford producing. It was Hot's lead singer Gwen Owens who requested the group be given a country song, and Ivey and Woodford obliged with "Angel in Your Arms", whose third co-writer was Muscle Shoals resident Tom (Tommy) Brasfield.

 Although Hot was officially a trio consisting of Owens, Cathy Carson, and Juanita Curiel, Owens has stated that she recorded "Angel in Your Arms" with only Carson as background vocalist: Irene Cathaway, with whom Owens and Carson had been performing and who was expected to record with them at Muscle Shoals, was a no-show at the recording studio, and "Angel in Your Arms" was recorded prior to the recruitment of Curiel as Cathaway's replacement.  Ivey played keyboards on Hot's recording of "Angel in Your Arms", which featured Mac McAnally on guitar.
At the time of Hot's success with their single version, the group also recorded a Spanish-language version entitled "Angel en Tus Brazos".

sections.heading: Chart history
sections.wikitext:
Picked up by [[Big Tree Records]], "Angel in Your Arms" accrued sufficient airplay by February 1977 to enter the [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]], entering the Pop [[Top 40]] that April to peak that July at #6; the track also charted R&B (#29) and Easy Listening (#9). ''Billboard'' ranked it as the [[Billboard Year-End Hot 100 singles of 1977|No. 5 song for 1977]]. Certified a [[RIAA certification|gold record]] for U.S. sales of one million units, "Angel in Your Arms" was also a hit for Hot in Australia (#27), Canada (#3) and New Zealand (#7). {| class="wikitable sortable" !Chart (1977) !Peak

sections.heading: C&W charting versions
sections.wikitext:
*The success of Hot with "Angel in Your Arms" brought an expedient cover aimed at the [[country radio|C&W market]] by Vivian Bell, a March 1977 release which failed to become a major hit with a #71 C&W peak.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.musicvf.com/song.php?id=112378 |title=The Angel in Your Arms (song by Vivian Bell) • Music VF, US & UK hits charts |website=Musicvf.com |date= |accessdate=2016-10-12}}</ref> 
*[[Robin Lee Bruce|Robin Lee]] recorded "Angel in Your Arms" in late 1982, the track originally serving as [[A-side and B-side|B-side]] of her inaugural single release "Turning Back the Covers" (#81 C&W): the single was re-released December 1982 with "Angel in Your Arms" as the [[A-side and B-side|A-side]] and as such more successful though still not a major hit with a #54 C&W peak. 
*"Angel in Your Arms" subsequently served as the B-side for two single releases by Lee: "I Heard It on the Radio" (#71 C&W) and the duet with [[Lobo (musician)|Lobo]]: "Paint the Town Blue" (#54 C&W).<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.musicvf.com/Robin+Lee.art |title=Robin Lee Songs • Top Songs / Chart Singles Discography • Music VF, US & UK hits charts |website=Musicvf.com |date= |accessdate=2016-10-12}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|author= |url=http://countrydiscoghraphy2.blogspot.ca/2014/06/robin-lee.html |title=Praguefrank's Country Discography 2: Robin Lee |website=Countrydiscoghraphy2.blogspot.ca |date=2014-06-10 |accessdate=2016-10-12}}</ref>
*[[Barbara Mandrell]], who had scored a 1982 #1 C&W hit with Brasfield's "Till You're Gone", recorded "Angel in Your Arms" in June 1985 in [[Nashville, Tennessee|Nashville]] to serve as an advance single from the album ''[[Get to the Heart]]'', marking the first newly recorded release by Mandrell after her 11 September 1984 automobile accident. A thematic return by Mandrell to the connubial concerns prevalent in her early hits, including her 1978 career record "[[(If Loving You Is Wrong) I Don't Want to Be Right]]", "Angel in Your Arms" reached #8 C&W.<ref name="Praguefrank">{{cite web |url=https://countrydiscography.blogspot.com/search/label/Mandrell%20Barbara |title=Praguefrank |accessdate=15 February 2010}}</ref>
sections.text:
*The success of Hot with "Angel in Your Arms" brought an expedient cover aimed at the C&W market by Vivian Bell, a March 1977 release which failed to become a major hit with a #71 C&W peak. 
*Robin Lee recorded "Angel in Your Arms" in late 1982, the track originally serving as B-side of her inaugural single release "Turning Back the Covers" (#81 C&W): the single was re-released December 1982 with "Angel in Your Arms" as the A-side and as such more successful though still not a major hit with a #54 C&W peak. 
*"Angel in Your Arms" subsequently served as the B-side for two single releases by Lee: "I Heard It on the Radio" (#71 C&W) and the duet with Lobo: "Paint the Town Blue" (#54 C&W).
*Barbara Mandrell, who had scored a 1982 #1 C&W hit with Brasfield's "Till You're Gone", recorded "Angel in Your Arms" in June 1985 in Nashville to serve as an advance single from the album Get to the Heart, marking the first newly recorded release by Mandrell after her 11 September 1984 automobile accident. A thematic return by Mandrell to the connubial concerns prevalent in her early hits, including her 1978 career record "(If Loving You Is Wrong) I Don't Want to Be Right", "Angel in Your Arms" reached #8 C&W.

sections.heading: Other versions
sections.wikitext:
"Angel in Your Arms" has also been recorded by: 
*[[Lynn Anderson]] (''[[I Love What Love Is Doing to Me/He Ain't You|I Love What Love Is Doing to Me]]'' 1977), 
*[[Red Hurley]] (as "The Angel in Your Arms") (''With Love'' 1978)
*[[Millie Jackson]] (''Feelin' Bitchy'' 1977)
*[[Reba McEntire]] (''[[Reba McEntire (album)|Reba McEntire]]'' 1977)
*[[Billie Jo Spears]] (''[[I Will Survive (Billie Jo Spears album)|I Will Survive]]'' 1979).<ref name="AMG"/> 
*In the UK, where the Hot's original recording had an unsuccessful April 1977 release, "Angel in Your Arms" was recorded in 1979 by veteran vocalist [[Carol Deene]] who had been inactive for some years: Deene's version, released on her own Koala label, failed to effect a chart comeback. 
*"Angel in Your Arms" was one of a number of tracks recorded in the spring of 2009 at [[Muscle Shoals Sound Studio]] by Queen Emily; Wolf Stephenson produced the sessions which featured Clayton Ivey on keyboards. The ''Queen Emily'' album was released in the UK in December 2010. 
*A Finnish rendering: "Älä Kysy Kuka On Sylissäin", was recorded by [[Vicky Rosti|Vicky]] for her 1978 album ''Tee Mulle Niin''.
